title: Offensive Hebrew Corpus and Detection using BERT
measurement_description: The paper measures the performance of pre-trained Hebrew language models (HeBERT and AlephBERT) on binary offensive language detection. The curated dataset categorizes hate speech, violence, and abusive language, which includes tracking targets of offensive language based on religion, race, and nationality (e.g., hate against Jews, Muslims, Druze).
base_benchmarks: DOLaH (Dataset of Offensive Language in Hebrew)
findings: The study found that offensive content in Hebrew is widespread, specifically targeting Arabs, Palestinians, and ethnoreligious groups like Jews and Muslims. When fine-tuning models on the compiled Hebrew dataset, AlephBERT generally outperformed HeBERT on most dataset configurations. However, combining the new data with the existing DOLaH benchmark boosted HeBERT's accuracy by 2% (up to 81%), while AlephBERT showed better generalizability when fine-tuned on the new data and tested on unseen datasets.
